procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 13.05.2008 of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in I. T. A. No. 544 of 2007
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Revenue went in appeal before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (in short ‘the Tribunal’) as well as before the High Court but the same got dismissed vide orders dated 23.02.2007 and 13.05.2008 respectively
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Revenue approached the Supreme Court by way of special leave after the High Court dismissed their appeal.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: When a bench of judges finds that a decision rendered by a bench of the same strength requires re-consideration, the matter should be directed to be placed before the Chief Justice of India for appropriate orders, such as constituting a larger bench.
obiter: The issue of deduction of export incentives by a supporting manufacturer under Section 80HHC of the IT Act is not identical to, and cannot be related with, the issues decided in certain other precedent cases.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court dismissed the appeals because the common question of law raised had already been definitively answered in favor of the assessee and against the Department by a prior decision of the Court in CIT v. Baby Marine Exports.
legal_tests_applied: Stare decisis / Adherence to binding precedent
why_appellant_lost: The question of law raised by the appellant (the Department) has been answered against them in the case of CIT v. Baby Marine Exports [2007] 290 ITR 323/160 Taxman 160.
The precedent set in CIT v. Baby Marine Exports was followed by another Bench of the Court in Commissioner of Income Tax Karnal vs. Sushil Kumar Gupta.
why_respondent_won: The question of law has been answered in favour of the assessee by the precedent set in CIT v. Baby Marine Exports [2007] 290 ITR 323/160 Taxman 160.
